newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday due to a technical correction on the domestic A share markets, which depressed demand on the repo markket, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract fell to 3.0 percent from 6.72 percent on Thursday. Combined volume of the six-contract market fell to 2.67 million from 5.39 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the A share market correction pushed the early-maturing contracts down in early trading and institutional selling in the afternoon also depressed the late-maturing ones.
Traders said they expected the repo rates to recover early next week if the A share markets perform better.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board with sentiment strengthened on the approach of interest payment day of a key contract, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, rose to 118.17 yuan from 117.28 yuan.
The first of the annual interest payments on the contract, issued in June last year, will be paid shortly. Most other contracts on the market have coupons payable only on maturity.

"The bond's first interest payment date is drawing near and its price is not matched with its yields," said one trader. "This has led to buying in the contract and follow-up buying in other contracts on Friday."
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 2.95 million lots from 2.57 million lots.

Traders said the market was also boosted on Friday by rumours that the central bank would possibly cut bank interest rates and due to lower coupons for the latest batch of state issue starting March 1. "Sentiment is good and the contracts are likely to continue to rise in the short term," said a trader.
